messages.subject: BSM run error
parts:
Hi all,
When I'm running BSM script I got this error, although I used the same script with small tree and it ran smoothly without any error but now I when used big data tree then got this error:

Error in if (.Platform$GUI != "AQUA" && ((is.na(num_cores_to_use) == TRUE) ||  : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

would you guys help me in removing this error.
Thank you,
Best,
Uz

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] BSM run error
parts:
My best guess is your big data script has left out some key line, either the source() commands, or e.g.:
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$num_cores_to_use = 1

If you had something like:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object$num_cores_to_use = NULL

...that could cause this error.


You can also check if:

.Platform$GUI != "AQUA"

...returns TRUE or FALSE. "AQUA" is a way of checking for R.app on Macs, which cannot use some of the multicore functionality.

Cheers,
Nick

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] BSM run error
parts:
Hi Uzma:

1. No, this is something very simple, the error message tells you that. Those are run settings, they have nothing to do with your data.

1.5. To get serious help from people on the internet, you have to HELP THEM.  To diagnose an issue, you have to provide all of the data files, and the exact script you are running, that caused the problem.  Otherwise, the people trying to help you are just making random guesses, and you are wasting their time. If you send everything I can take a look, but I am traveling this week.

2. Here's my guess, but it's just a guess: Since it's simple, it's probably some error in setting up your script and/or copying/pasting it into R.  The most likely thing is failing to do things in this order, and RE-DO THEM AFTER EACH TIME YOU START R:

====================
# CRUCIAL CRUCIAL CRUCIAL: 
# YOU HAVE TO RUN THE SOURCE COMMANDS AFTER 
# *EVERY TIME* YOU DO library(BioGeoBEARS). THE CHANGES ARE NOT "PERMANENT", 
# THEY HAVE TO BE MADE EACH TIME.  IF YOU ARE GOING TO BE OFFLINE, 
# YOU CAN DOWNLOAD EACH .R FILE TO YOUR HARD DRIVE AND REFER THE source()
# COMMANDS TO THE FULL PATH AND FILENAME OF EACH FILE ON YOUR
# LOCAL SYSTEM INSTEAD.
########################################################
library(BioGeoBEARS)
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/cladoRcpp.R") # (needed now that traits model added; source FIRST!)
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_add_fossils_randomly_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_basics_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_calc_transition_matrices_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_classes_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_detection_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_DNA_cladogenesis_sim_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_extract_Qmat_COOmat_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_generics_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_models_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_on_multiple_trees_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_plots_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_readwrite_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_simulate_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_SSEsim_makePlots_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_SSEsim_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_stochastic_mapping_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_stratified_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_univ_model_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/calc_uppass_probs_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/calc_loglike_sp_v01.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/get_stratified_subbranch_top_downpass_likelihoods_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/runBSM_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/stochastic_map_given_inputs.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/summarize_BSM_tables_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_traits_v1.R") # added traits model
calc_loglike_sp = compiler::cmpfun(calc_loglike_sp_prebyte)    # crucial to fix bug in uppass calculations
calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch = compiler::cmpfun(calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch_prebyte)
    # slight speedup hopefully

====================

Cheers,
Nick

parts:
Hi Uzma,

Apologies for slow replies, I've been travelling. I took a look at your script.  It looks to me like you are using some old version or have modified version.



SHORT VERSION OF THE PROBLEM:

Make sure that the input "res", on this line:

==========
stochastic_mapping_inputs_list = get_inputs_for_stochastic_mapping(res=res)
==========

...is actually a full results object from "bears_optim_run".  

You instead had modified "res" via this line:

=============
res = plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object, analysis_titletxt, addl_params=list("j"), plotwhat="text", label.offset=0.45, tipcex=0.7, statecex=0.7, splitcex=0.6, titlecex=0.8, plotsplits=TRUE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir, include_null_range=TRUE, tr=tr, tipranges=tipranges)
=============

So that "res" only included:

===============
> res
        LnL nparams         d     e j
1 -367.0797       2 0.3822085 1e-12 0
===============

This modified "res" has none of the necessary inputs for Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping.


In the actual BSM example script at:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeographical-stochastic-mapping-example-script#BSM_script

The line is "res2 = plot_BioGeoBEARS_results..." ...so that you can use "res" later on.



ATTACHMENT

The attached script fixes the issue, by using "resDEC" for all inputs.  You could (more simply) just have the script say 

res = resDEC 

...and then use "res2 = plot_BioGeoBEARS_results..." when you want to plot the ML state estimates.






LESSON:

All good use of R is an *active* process.  By typing in the names of variables like "res" and seeing what they hold, many of these sort of minor problems can be solved by the user -- you just have to treat R as a tool you are using, not as a black box!








LONGER VERSION FOR CONTEXT:

The results object, in the example scripts, gets names like "res", "resDEC", "resDECj", etc. -- PAY ATTENTION TO WHICH RES OBJECT YOU WANT TO DO BSM ON!!!!!!   There is little point in doing BSM on DEC if DEC+J had a much better fit!

The results should have all kinds of things in it, which you will see if you:

- type "res" and hit return
- type names(res) for a summary of what's in there.  For example, it should look like this:

==============
 [1] "computed_likelihoods_at_each_node"                                
 [2] "relative_probs_of_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node_DOWNPASS"      
 [3] "condlikes_of_each_state"                                          
 [4] "relative_probs_of_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node_DOWNPASS"
 [5] "relative_probs_of_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node_UPPASS"  
 [6] "relative_probs_of_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node_UPPASS"        
 [7] "ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node"          
 [8] "ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node"                
 [9] "relative_probs_of_each_state_at_bottom_of_root_branch"            
[10] "total_loglikelihood"                                              
[11] "inputs"                                                           
[12] "outputs"                                                          
[13] "optim_result" 
==============

You will find that res$inputs has the original run settings that you put into the BioGeoBEARS_run_object.

You will also find that "res$inputs$num_cores_to_use" stores the number of cores that you want to use.

I think you had an error like this:

==============
Error in if (num_cores_to_use > 1) { : argument is of length zero
==============


This happened, because when you called this function:

================
get_inputs_for_stochastic_mapping(res=res)
================

...this contains the line:

================
num_cores_to_use = res$inputs$num_cores_to_use
================

...but if res is just:

===============
> res
        LnL nparams         d     e j
1 -367.0797       2 0.3822085 1e-12 0
===============


Then there is no res$inputs$num_cores_to_use at all, so res$inputs$num_cores_to_use is NULL, so num_cores_to_use, so the if/then conditional argument "(num_cores_to_use > 1)" is length zero, instead of TRUE or FALSE.  Statements of "if" require TRUE or FALSE, so this error makes sense:

==============
Error in if (num_cores_to_use > 1) { : argument is of length zero
==============

Cheers,
Nick

PS: I've got it running now...

...that could cause this error.


You can also check if:

.Platform$GUI != "AQUA"

...returns TRUE or FALSE. "AQUA" is a way of checking for R.app on Macs, which cannot use some of the multicore functionality.

Cheers,
Nick
